title: Moving Day
lines: Last box and then I'm buying the pizza.
Deal. This couch is a beast though.
I don't think it's going to fit.
It's so thick I can barely get my hands around it.
Ugh, it's not going in straight.
Tilt it a little and shove.
God, it's really deep once it finally goes in.
Almost there… just a little more.
Okay it's in. Damn, that took forever.
Yeah, I usually finish a lot faster than that.

title: The Scenic Route
lines: We've been in the driveway for three minutes, turn this shit off.
I like to set the mood early.
Fair. Map says left at the end of the street.
This road looks way too tight.
Alright, I'll take it slow. Just tell me if I get close to anything.
Slow down… you're coming in too fast.
The clearance is really low. You might have to take the top off.
Smart. Keep us in the middle.
There's barely any room to move in here.
Just keep calling the sides for me.
A little more left… okay, good.
We're past the worst of it.
Wait, I think it's going to overflow.
Hold on, I've got the cup.
Holy shit, still in the driveway apparently.

title: Bake Sale
lines: Bake sale starts in an hour. How's the batter?
Sticky as hell. Don't touch it yet.
I already washed my hands twice.
This is way thicker than I expected. I can barely work it.
Add a little liquid and keep folding.
I think I put too much filling inside. It's starting to bulge.
Yes. Twist the top so nothing comes back out.
The bag is so hard to squeeze. My hand is getting tired.
Grip higher up. That should help.
Keep the tip close to the surface.
It's leaking everywhere. I can't stop it.
Let it sit a second before you add another layer.
Nice. Look at that rise. Perfect little peak.
Price tags and we're out of here.
And one for quality control, obviously.

title: Gym Spotter
lines: Alright, last set on bench. You ready?
Yeah. Just don't drop it on me.
I won't. How many are we aiming for?
This bar is heavier than it looks. I can barely get it up.
It's not going all the way down. There's too much resistance.
Lower it slow. Control the weight.
My arms are shaking. I don't think I can finish.
Almost there. Just a little lower.
Okay, got it. Spot me on the way up.
Racked. That last rep felt endless.
Yeah, you were really struggling to get it all the way in.
Or you just need better form when you're under pressure.
Water, then stretch. My shoulders are cooked.

title: Camping Tent
lines: This tent is supposed to be a two-person. Feels tight already.
Just crawl in and I'll zip us up.
It's under the bag. I'll grab it.
I can't get the pole all the way through this sleeve.
Wiggle it a bit. It should slide once you find the right angle.
It's stuck halfway. There's no more give.
Try pushing from your side a bit more.
Okay, it's in. Now the rainfly is bunched up.
Stretch it over the top and stake it down.
These stakes are refusing to go into the ground.
Rocky soil. Needs a firm hit.
As long as nothing unexpected comes in the middle of the night.
Yeah, it's going to get real close once we both settle in.
At least the view is nice.
Once the fly is secure, yes. Pass the snacks.

title: Office Printer
lines: This printer has been jamming all morning.
Did you try turning it off and on again?
Open the back and check the rollers.
The paper keeps getting stuck halfway through.
Open the tray and clear whatever's in there.
Pull it slow so you don't rip it.
It's really tight in there. I can barely reach.
Just feel around until you find the jam.
Now it's saying the toner is low.
Shake the cartridge and put it back in.
It won't seat properly. Something's blocking it.
Push until you hear the click.
Look at that. Clean output on the first try.
Remind me to order more paper.
And maybe a bigger tray. This one fills up way too fast.
Thanks. Back to actual work before I lose it.

title: Furniture Assembly
lines: These instructions are useless. Which screw is which?
The long ones go in the side panels first.
There are three lengths in this bag.
Ignore the shortest ones for now.
This hole is too small. The screw won't go in.
Try a different angle. Sometimes it just needs a better start.
It's starting to go but it's really tight.
My wrist is already sore from this.
Switch hands if you need to. Just get it done.
Now the shelf. It has to slide all the way to the back.
It's not seating flush. There's a gap.
Give it a firm shove. It should drop into place.
Good. Hardware for the doors next.
Not bad for something that fought us the whole time.

title: Kayak Launch
lines: Water looks calm. Ready to shove off?
Yeah. Hold the stern while I get in.
This cockpit is narrower than I remember.
Just lower yourself slowly. No rush.
My legs are stuck. I can't get them under the deck.
Wiggle a little. There's more space once you're sitting.
Okay, I'm in. Hand me the paddle.
Dip deep and pull clean. Long strokes.
Current's picking up near the bend.
The current is stronger than it looks out here.
Lean into it. Don't fight the water.
Hard left. Dig in and power through.
Made it. That was closer than I wanted.
Yeah, you almost went in sideways back there.
Next time we check the flow rate.
Agreed. My arms are already toast.

title: Late-Night Coding
lines: Show me the stack. Maybe I can spot it.
You're not checking the return value.
It works fine until I try to pass a bigger load.
You're overflowing the buffer. Need to handle larger inputs.
I thought the limit was high enough.
I already increased the size. Still choking.
Try breaking it into smaller chunks.
While you're in there, clean up the nested ifs.
Now it's hanging. Just spinning forever.
Looks like an infinite loop. You never told it when to stop.
Fixed the exit condition. Testing again.
Yeah, the last part is really slow to complete.
Optimize the inner loop. You're doing extra work for no reason.
Pushed the commit. Pray it passes CI.
If it fails again I'm going to lose it.

title: Pottery Class
lines: Okay, center the clay. Keep it wet.
More water. And slower wheel speed.
You need more pressure from the outside.
Good. Now cone it up and down a couple times.
Yes. Now open it up slowly. Don't go too wide too fast.
Support the walls while you pull up.
I'll try to even it out.
Steady hands. Thin it out gradually.
I think I made the base too thick.
You can still fix it. Just compress and reshape.
Not bad for a first try. Nice even height.
I'm covered in slip. This is messier than I expected.
If you say so. Pass the towel.

title: Moving a Mattress
lines: This king is not going to make that corner.
Tip it vertical. We'll walk it through.
Yeah, should help with the walls.
It's too wide. We're stuck halfway.
Angle it more. Push from your end.
A little higher on your side.
I can't get any leverage. My grip keeps slipping.
Wrap your arms around it better.
Watch the railing. Don't scrape the walls.
Almost clear. Just the last bit.
Now the generational trauma of putting the bed frame together.
That took way longer than it should have.
Or buy a smaller bed. This one is ridiculous.
Absolutely. My back is already yelling.

title: Bread Dough
lines: Dough's been rising for an hour. Time to shape.
It's sticky as hell. Keeps clinging to my fingers.
Dust with more flour and fold it over.
Every time I press down it springs right back.
Be firm. Show it who's boss.
The surface is tearing. I think I overworked it.
Let it rest a minute then try again.
Steam it well or the crust won't open up right.
Twenty minutes in and it's barely colored.
Give it more time. You don't want a pale finish.
Yeah. When it finally comes out it's going to be worth the wait.

title: IKEA Closet
lines: This wardrobe has more pieces than a spaceship.
Start with the side panels. Long bolts first.
Cam locks in one pile, dowels in another.
This cam lock won't catch. It just spins.
Push the dowel all the way in before you turn.
Make sure the arrow faces the hole.
Still nothing. Feels like it's not engaging.
Harder. You have to seat it all the way.
Hold it steady while I drive these screws.
The back panel is warping. It won't sit flat.
Force it into the groove from the top down.
Align the hinges carefully or they'll never close right.
Good enough. I'm not opening that thing again today.
And never again without the power screwdriver. My hands are done.
